{{recipe}}

'''Steamed rice''' is a simple dish, but some individuals have trouble cooking it. Common issues include adding too much rice or water, and not following the package directions. This recipe for steamed rice is fail-safe and does not require the use of a special rice cooker or microwave.

==Ingredients==
*1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (250 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] or 8.5 fl oz) dry [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]]
*2 cups water
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] (optional)

==Procedure==
# Wash the rice if desired.
#Place the rice in a deep [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]] with lid. Add salt if using, and stir.
#Bring rice to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] over high heat. Stir.
#Reduce heat to low and cover the pot. Cook on low for 12 minutes.
#Uncover rice and serve.

== Visual procedure ==
<gallery mode="packed">
File:Steamed Rice How to 01.jpg|1. Fill cup with desired amount of rice.
File:Steamed Rice How to 02.jpg|2. Pour rice into saucepan (mix optional salt in at this point).
File:Steamed Rice How to 03.jpg|3. Pour water into saucepan. Remember—twice as much water as rice.
File:Steamed Rice How to 04.jpg|4. Stir water so that floating rice sinks.
File:Steamed Rice How to 05.jpg|5. Place saucepan on stove and set temperature to "high". Do not cover.
File:Steamed Rice How to 06.jpg|6. Wait until water begins to boil.
File:Steamed Rice How to 07.jpg|7. Stir rice again.
File:Steamed Rice How to 08.jpg|8. Set temperature to lowest setting. Cover saucepan with lid.
File:Steamed Rice How to 09.jpg|9. After twelve minutes turn the element off and uncover. The rice is ready to eat.
</gallery>

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* This formula can be easily scaled up or down. The universal rule with cooking steamed rice is that the proportion of water should be double that of the rice. If you use one cup of rice you must use two cups of water. If you use two cups of rice you must use four cups of water.
* 1 cup dry rice is enough for three adults.
